AI infrastructure supply-demand gapAI基础设施供需缺口
×13 · 50 steps
AI infrastructure supply is structurally constrained vs exponential demand growth. Global AI compute power demand is projected to rise from 83 GW in 2023 to 532 GW by 2031, but supply only from 39 GW to 253 GW, leaving a widening gap. Hyperscaler capex surged 87% Y/Y and is expected to remain elevated (~$1.2 tn in 2027), driving tightness in data center capacity, memory, cooling, and power infrastructure. US data center construction is limited by labor to 12–35 GW/year, while TSMC, Intel, and ASML ramp equipment capacity by 30%+. AI contract pricing is rising 25% on renewals, and CoreWeave backlog reached $104 bn. AI debt issuance is straining credit markets, with spreads widening 30 bp YTD.

  1. 1
    Premise
    The global memory market is under extreme pressure as AI infrastructure buildouts compete for the same DRAM and NAND supply as consumer hardware, with GS Semiconductor analysts forecasting ~316% growth in conventional DRAM pricing in 2026E and a 256% increase in NAND pricing in 2026, with the supply/demand mismatch expected to persist through 2028.

Nomura4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    The end of Moore's law dynamics: producing chips now requires extreme ultraviolet lithography tools costing upwards of USD200mn each, shipped in limited numbers by a single supplier (ASML), and each new manufacturing process begins with a low yield that takes longer to raise with every generation.
    d77061cadbb7·《Chipnomics: Introducing Nomura's Chip Shortage Index》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    The 'memory wall' bottleneck: HBM requires several times as much silicon area per functional bit as commodity DRAM, and stacking and through-silicon-via processes have materially lower yields, so every line converted to HBM removes conventional memory capacity from the market; memory chip export prices surged by 135% y-o-y on average in H1 2026.
    d77061cadbb7·《Chipnomics: Introducing Nomura's Chip Shortage Index》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The current supercycle is structural: since Q4 2025 AI and HBM demand have become large enough and sufficiently wafer-intensive to tighten deliverable supply; both decomposition components are now positive, and the CSI contribution has risen more sharply and become the larger driver, with inventories across the supply chain remaining historically low.
    d77061cadbb7·《Chipnomics: Introducing Nomura's Chip Shortage Index》·2026-08-20
  4. 4
    Call
    RatingBoom / deep shortage — sustained
    Global semiconductor / memory chip cycle: rating Boom / deep shortage — sustained
    d77061cadbb7·《Chipnomics: Introducing Nomura's Chip Shortage Index》·2026-08-20

Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    On-budget fiscal revenue growth rose further to +11.7% yoy in July from +8.7% yoy in June despite lower PPI inflation and weaker activity growth, led by faster tax revenue growth to +13.9% yoy from +10.8% yoy, while non-tax revenue growth slowed to -5.4% yoy from +2.9% yoy; corporate income tax revenue growth remained elevated at 22% yoy in July, and anecdotal evidence suggests fiscally strained local governments have tightened tax collection recently.

    Mechanism

China fiscal & infrastructure push中国财政与基础设施刺激
×6 · 22 steps
China's government is accelerating fiscal spending and infrastructure investment after the July Politburo pivot. An RMB800bn policy-based financial instrument was announced, local government bond issuance is picking up, and the 15th Five-Year Plan targets 60,000km high-speed rail by 2030. Consumption support includes 18 measures for lower-tier cities and visa-free tourism expansion. However, government bond issuance still trails last year's pace, and property policy easing remains incremental.
9 extracted · 7 firms
Consensus·7 firms·9 extracted·As of 2026-08-21
China is accelerating fiscal spending and infrastructure investment post-July Politburo, but fixed-asset investment and property data remain weak, suggesting slow policy transmission.中国在7月政治局会议后加速财政支出和基础设施投资，但固定资产投资和地产数据仍然疲弱，显示政策传导缓慢。
Overall, analysts characterize stimulus as measured and unlikely to drive a sharp turnaround, with bond issuance still trailing last year's pace.总体而言，分析师认为刺激措施力度温和，不太可能推动急剧转机，债券发行仍慢于去年速度。

Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Hatzius says GS does not expect the Fed to hike, largely because much of the recent strength in core PCE inflation reflects temporary factors: higher oil prices related to the US-Iran war, roughly 70bp of lingering tariff pass-through, and distortions in software and accessories prices; GS expects core inflation to move close to 2% in 2027.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Hatzius argues that markets price what they think the Fed will do, not what they think the Fed should do; if the Fed obscures its reaction function, market guesses about the Fed's next moves will simply become worse, leading to more volatility that serves no constructive economic purpose.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    After two months of materially softer jobs and inflation data, a hike at the September meeting has become very unlikely barring a dramatic shift in the tone of the August data due in early September; under our baseline economic forecasts the inflation news is more likely to improve further than to deteriorate anew as the year progresses, and we still think market pricing for the funds rate is too hawkish.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17
  4. 4
    Call
    Our rates strategists expect the US Treasury curve to steepen further on better inflation news, reduced hike premium, and troubling budget news; great Q2 earnings and a stabilization in the AI trade have helped equity markets make new highs, and our equity strategists expect the major indices to continue trending higher into yearend.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17
Nomura5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Nomura continues to expect the Fed to remain on hold, with recent CPI/PPI pointing to benign core PCE and softer employment/retail data easing overheating concerns.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Since 1990 there has been no hawkish pivot (a policy move opposite to the previous action) in H2 of an election year, and tightening actions including rate hikes, QT, and QE tapering have been relatively uncommon at the October and November meetings prior to national elections.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    Quantitative tightening is a central element of the Warsh Fed's anti-inflation policy; Warsh attributes five years of above-target inflation to the Fed's failure to mop up QE-era liquidity, and QT could lift long-term rates without raising the policy rate.
    3805c7024e31·《How will Japan and US address the risks of inflation and falling behind the curve?》·2026-08-19
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Economic data and the timing of midterm elections are likely to lead to a near-term hold for the next four months, which could ultimately extend into an indefinite hold if the economy and inflation evolve as Nomura expects; by year-end 2026 the Fed will have substantially more inflation data, which Nomura expects will strengthen confidence in sustained disinflation.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20

Goldman Sachs5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Etsy has intentionally positioned itself to be a share taker and first mover as the world increasingly shifts towards agentic commerce both through off-platform partnerships and innovating toward AI increasingly at the center of the consumer experience on property; in 4Q25, management noted that traffic from LLMs, although small, was 15x higher in 2025 vs 2024, signaling the rapid shift in how buyers are discovering the platform; this traffic converts at a higher rate than traditional media referrals as AI-originated traffic are often high intent customers; management has also noted Etsy's unique inventory is additive to LLMs as it is not commoditized or mass-produced like other online players.
    6d510db1ec8e·《The Post Depop Etsy Emerges; Updating Our Operating Estimates & Framing Key Debates; Reinstate Rating at Neutral (PT of $89)》·2026-08-17
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Etsy is positioning AI agents as an incremental discovery channel for unique inventory that is difficult to find through traditional search (aligning to their key priority of showing up where the shopper is); management has repeatedly framed agentic shopping as an opportunity rather than a disintermediation risk; to improve visibility across emerging AI-driven discovery channels, Etsy has invested in enhancing listing quality and marketplace data structure — encouraging more descriptive and conversational product titles and descriptions, improving product imagery, and introducing additional mandatory listing attributes — to create richer product metadata enabling LLMs and recommendation systems to better understand inventory and match products with relevant buyer intent.
    6d510db1ec8e·《The Post Depop Etsy Emerges; Updating Our Operating Estimates & Framing Key Debates; Reinstate Rating at Neutral (PT of $89)》·2026-08-17
  3. 3
    Mechanism

    6d510db1ec8e·《The Post Depop Etsy Emerges; Updating Our Operating Estimates & Framing Key Debates; Reinstate Rating at Neutral (PT of $89)》·2026-08-17

    6d510db1ec8e·《The Post Depop Etsy Emerges; Updating Our Operating Estimates & Framing Key Debates; Reinstate Rating at Neutral (PT of $89)》·2026-08-17

Logic Chains by Firm5 firms · 19 steps · every step verified verbatim against the source
J.P. Morgan5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    A model sits on the Pareto frontier when peers cannot provide higher capability at the same or lower price, or comparable capability more cheaply; models inside the curve face a harder commercial position as users can choose a stronger or cheaper alternative.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    JPMorgan currently favors the intelligence/capability end of the frontier because intelligence is still advancing rapidly and stronger models are relatively insulated from weaker alternatives' pricing, while mature intelligence is increasingly supplied by more providers, so sustainable cost leadership requires structural efficiency rather than aggressive pricing.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    DeepSeek is the clearest Chinese example of structural cost leadership, with low pricing supported by model architecture and system-level efficiency across MoE, attention design, KV-cache requirements, quantization and serving optimization, giving it flexibility to decide how much efficiency improvement to pass through to users and how much to retain through monetization.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    JPMorgan prefers Zhipu over MiniMax because Zhipu's latest competitive improvement (GLM-5.3) is internally generated and more defensible, whereas MiniMax's near-term improvement comes from a competitor's DeepSeek repricing decision and can reverse; Zhipu's thesis requires continued model iteration rather than relying on GLM-5.3 alone.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  5. 5
    Call
    MaintainOverweightTarget price1600 → 1800 HKD
    Z AI Co Ltd (Zhipu AI): rating Overweight (prior Overweight); target 1600 → 1800 HKD; reference 1270
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18

Deutsche Bank3 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Over the past decade, China has undertaken one of the most significant monetary policy framework reforms among major economies, transitioning from a quantity-based framework toward a more market-based one across four phases: pre-2015 quantity framework, 2015-2019 interest-rate liberalization, 2019-2024 MLF-linked LPR system, and 2024 onward transition to overnight repo.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Monetary policy modernization in China has been less about replacing quantitative tools with policy rates than about rebalancing their relative importance, with market-based interest rates now playing an increasing role in policy implementation and transmission while structural and quantitative instruments continue to support broader policy objectives and financial stability considerations.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    China has moved substantially towards a more interest-rate-centric framework, but the transition remains incomplete — the interest-rate corridor is still evolving, multiple policy objectives continue to shape implementation, and quantitative as well as structural tools remain important alongside policy rates; the next phase of reform is likely to focus less on building new instruments and more on improving how policy signals are transmitted through financial markets and the broader economy.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20

Bernstein4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    The AI buildout is threatening affordability and reliability for consumers; rate increases tied to new data center load have caused electricity prices to rise, and grid operators are flagging interconnection queues and capacity constraints that read, to a consumer, as a reliability risk even before an outage actually happens.
    671dbe7d182d·《Energy & Power: Loss, not change, is what we're actually afraid of...》·2026-08-22
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    At the federal level, the framing is almost entirely national security; the dominant argument for pushing data center buildout through, even over local objection, is that losing the AI race to China is an existential threat and security risk, and that argument is explicitly being used to justify preempting local rate cases and permitting fights.
    671dbe7d182d·《Energy & Power: Loss, not change, is what we're actually afraid of...》·2026-08-22
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Most contested energy infrastructure eventually gets built, from rural power lines to interstate transmission; the data center fight isn't an exception to how energy transitions normally go, just a faster, more compressed version of the same negotiation, happening in public and in real time, because change is hard and someone, somewhere, is always being asked to absorb a real loss first and trust that the benefit arrives later.

BernsteinDissent3 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940, in combo with Keytruda), met both the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and the key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival in a Ph3 melanoma trial, representing the first successful late stage validation of a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine platform.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Melanoma alone is unlikely to become a mega-blockbuster market - more likely low single-digit billions; however, if efficacy can be replicated in NSCLC, RCC, bladder cancer and earlier-stage solid tumors, personalized neoantigen vaccines could evolve from a ~$1-2 Bn melanoma opportunity into a platform exceeding $10 Bn across multiple solid tumor indications.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The key challenge is reproducing melanoma success in other tumor types - melanoma is among the most immunogenic cancers with high tumor mutational burden and abundant neoantigens; the true test will be indications such as NSCLC, RCC, bladder cancer, and eventually colder tumors with lower mutation burdens like CRC, where generating a sufficiently strong immune response may be more difficult.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21

    Mechanism

    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Reusable launch systems, smaller satellites, advances in computing and modern manufacturing techniques have fundamentally shifted the economics of reaching space, allowing private-sector companies to build infrastructure once exclusive to government programs while capital markets provide critical funding.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The report's key data project $1.4tn in global commercial space revenue by 2030, $700bn in global value from Earth observation data by 2035, a 25x reduction in launch costs since 1981, 600+ global ground stations, 65% of economic value generated by GPS since 1980 and 3.9x growth in space-launched objects since 2010.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18

Fiscal Sustainability Fears: US Debt Trajectory and Monetary Policy Uncertainty
Elevated US debt-to-GDP ratio (over $40 trillion) is highlighted in social media and opinion pieces as a structural driver of market stress. Concerns over a potential shift to state-funded Medicare and the risk of quantitative easing due to trade war fallout add to fiscal angst. The debate centers on whether the Fed will be forced into accommodation, which would support gold and long bonds, versus the risk of higher yields if credibility is lost. The Jackson Hole symposium, featuring Chair Warsh's keynote, is the immediate catalyst for assessing the Fed's stance on these fiscal-monetary interactions.

Nomura4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Nomura continues to expect the Fed to remain on hold, with recent CPI/PPI pointing to benign core PCE and softer employment/retail data easing overheating concerns.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Since 1990 there has been no hawkish pivot (a policy move opposite to the previous action) in H2 of an election year, and tightening actions including rate hikes, QT, and QE tapering have been relatively uncommon at the October and November meetings prior to national elections.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    Quantitative tightening is a central element of the Warsh Fed's anti-inflation policy; Warsh attributes five years of above-target inflation to the Fed's failure to mop up QE-era liquidity, and QT could lift long-term rates without raising the policy rate.
    3805c7024e31·《How will Japan and US address the risks of inflation and falling behind the curve?》·2026-08-19
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Economic data and the timing of midterm elections are likely to lead to a near-term hold for the next four months, which could ultimately extend into an indefinite hold if the economy and inflation evolve as Nomura expects; by year-end 2026 the Fed will have substantially more inflation data, which Nomura expects will strengthen confidence in sustained disinflation.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20

Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Hatzius says GS does not expect the Fed to hike, largely because much of the recent strength in core PCE inflation reflects temporary factors: higher oil prices related to the US-Iran war, roughly 70bp of lingering tariff pass-through, and distortions in software and accessories prices; GS expects core inflation to move close to 2% in 2027.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Hatzius argues that markets price what they think the Fed will do, not what they think the Fed should do; if the Fed obscures its reaction function, market guesses about the Fed's next moves will simply become worse, leading to more volatility that serves no constructive economic purpose.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    After two months of materially softer jobs and inflation data, a hike at the September meeting has become very unlikely barring a dramatic shift in the tone of the August data due in early September; under our baseline economic forecasts the inflation news is more likely to improve further than to deteriorate anew as the year progresses, and we still think market pricing for the funds rate is too hawkish.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17
  4. 4
    Call
    Our rates strategists expect the US Treasury curve to steepen further on better inflation news, reduced hike premium, and troubling budget news; great Q2 earnings and a stabilization in the AI trade have helped equity markets make new highs, and our equity strategists expect the major indices to continue trending higher into yearend.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17

    Quantitative tightening is a central element of the Warsh Fed's anti-inflation policy; Warsh attributes five years of above-target inflation to the Fed's failure to mop up QE-era liquidity, and QT could lift long-term rates without raising the policy rate.
    3805c7024e31·《How will Japan and US address the risks of inflation and falling behind the curve?》·2026-08-19
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Economic data and the timing of midterm elections are likely to lead to a near-term hold for the next four months, which could ultimately extend into an indefinite hold if the economy and inflation evolve as Nomura expects; by year-end 2026 the Fed will have substantially more inflation data, which Nomura expects will strengthen confidence in sustained disinflation.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
▼ShortFed policy uncertainty and US rate expectations
Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Hatzius says GS does not expect the Fed to hike, largely because much of the recent strength in core PCE inflation reflects temporary factors: higher oil prices related to the US-Iran war, roughly 70bp of lingering tariff pass-through, and distortions in software and accessories prices; GS expects core inflation to move close to 2% in 2027.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Hatzius argues that markets price what they think the Fed will do, not what they think the Fed should do; if the Fed obscures its reaction function, market guesses about the Fed's next moves will simply become worse, leading to more volatility that serves no constructive economic purpose.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    After two months of materially softer jobs and inflation data, a hike at the September meeting has become very unlikely barring a dramatic shift in the tone of the August data due in early September; under our baseline economic forecasts the inflation news is more likely to improve further than to deteriorate anew as the year progresses, and we still think market pricing for the funds rate is too hawkish.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17

    Call

  4. 4

US-Canada trade negotiations collapsed, triggering Trump's 50% tariffs on scores of Canadian imports (autos, steel, aluminum, wine, etc.) over the weekend.     355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20

    Mechanism

    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    Quantitative tightening is a central element of the Warsh Fed's anti-inflation policy; Warsh attributes five years of above-target inflation to the Fed's failure to mop up QE-era liquidity, and QT could lift long-term rates without raising the policy rate.
    3805c7024e31·《How will Japan and US address the risks of inflation and falling behind the curve?》·2026-08-19
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Economic data and the timing of midterm elections are likely to lead to a near-term hold for the next four months, which could ultimately extend into an indefinite hold if the economy and inflation evolve as Nomura expects; by year-end 2026 the Fed will have substantially more inflation data, which Nomura expects will strengthen confidence in sustained disinflation.
    355ed1806f36·《US - Election timing favors Fed patience》·2026-08-20
▼ShortFed policy uncertainty and US rate expectations
Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Hatzius says GS does not expect the Fed to hike, largely because much of the recent strength in core PCE inflation reflects temporary factors: higher oil prices related to the US-Iran war, roughly 70bp of lingering tariff pass-through, and distortions in software and accessories prices; GS expects core inflation to move close to 2% in 2027.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Hatzius argues that markets price what they think the Fed will do, not what they think the Fed should do; if the Fed obscures its reaction function, market guesses about the Fed's next moves will simply become worse, leading to more volatility that serves no constructive economic purpose.
    e6ae486ad7c4·《Assessing a Less Transparent Fed》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    After two months of materially softer jobs and inflation data, a hike at the September meeting has become very unlikely barring a dramatic shift in the tone of the August data due in early September; under our baseline economic forecasts the inflation news is more likely to improve further than to deteriorate anew as the year progresses, and we still think market pricing for the funds rate is too hawkish.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17

    Call
    Our rates strategists expect the US Treasury curve to steepen further on better inflation news, reduced hike premium, and troubling budget news; great Q2 earnings and a stabilization in the AI trade have helped equity markets make new highs, and our equity strategists expect the major indices to continue trending higher into yearend.

Iran 'Economic D-Day' Sanctions Escalate Geopolitical Risk
The Trump administration, led by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, unveiled a sweeping sanctions campaign against Iran dubbed 'Operation Economic Outcast' or 'Economic D-Day,' targeting oil revenue, shipping, banking, and secondary sanctions on enablers including China. The move follows the collapse of a 60-day ceasefire window and includes threats of further waves. Markets price in heightened risk of supply disruptions in the Persian Gulf, elevated oil prices, and a flight to safe havens. The aggressive rhetoric and lack of a clear sanctions roadmap add uncertainty, pressuring risk assets and boosting gold and the dollar.

QIs China's oil demand peaking due to economic slowdown?
▼ShortChina macro slowdown dampens demand across sectors
Goldman Sachs4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    On-budget fiscal revenue growth rose further to +11.7% yoy in July from +8.7% yoy in June despite lower PPI inflation and weaker activity growth, led by faster tax revenue growth to +13.9% yoy from +10.8% yoy, while non-tax revenue growth slowed to -5.4% yoy from +2.9% yoy; corporate income tax revenue growth remained elevated at 22% yoy in July, and anecdotal evidence suggests fiscally strained local governments have tightened tax collection recently.
    78aeb23a59de·《China: Strong fiscal revenue and slower spending led to a narrower deficit in July》·2026-08-23
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    July fiscal data suggest that policy support has not been significantly stepped up and fiscal policy has remained a growth drag in early Q3, despite further growth slowdown and stronger easing rhetoric from the July Politburo meeting, owing partly to the time required for policy coordination and local execution.
    78aeb23a59de·《China: Strong fiscal revenue and slower spending led to a narrower deficit in July》·2026-08-23
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Goldman expects the government to accelerate the pace of bond issuance and proceeds spending in coming months, speed up implementation of the new policy-based financial instrument, and keep the door open to additional easing later this year if growth slows further and the full-year growth target of '4.5-5.0%' comes under pressure; these expected policy efforts may help turn the fiscal impulse from a growth drag in Q2 to a modest driver in H2, though the pace could be more gradual than previously envisaged.
    78aeb23a59de·《China: Strong fiscal revenue and slower spending led to a narrower deficit in July》·2026-08-23
  4. 4
    Call
    Goldman continues to expect land sales revenue to decline by around 20% yoy this year, given the prolonged property downturn (especially for construction activity) and still-stretched funding conditions for many developers.
    78aeb23a59de·《China: Strong fiscal revenue and slower spending led to a narrower deficit in July》·2026-08-23

Trigger rule details
The three observed quantities
Sector relative strength = how far a sector's return has beaten the broad market's over the trailing quarter (a price proxy for crowding)
Market breadth = how many stocks participate in the rally (equal-weight index underperforming cap-weight = narrowing breadth)
% above 200-day MA = how far price sits above its own 200-day moving average (the standard BIAS technical indicator)
How the light is decided
🔴 Red: hottest sector's relative strength enters the top 5% of 10 years (≥95) AND market breadth narrows into the top 10% (≥90) — both must hold
🟡 Amber: relative strength ≥95 but breadth only to ≥60; or either relative strength or 200-day bias enters the top 1% (≥99)
🟢 Green: everything else
Once red has fired, it doesn't snap straight back to green: it must exit the top 20% (relative strength) or the top 60% (breadth) before returning to green, resting on amber in between (anti-flicker)
Any missing data shows “No data” — it never defaults to green
